summary: Sayadaw U Pandita was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Nandasiri Sayadaw. He was a meditation teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw from 1982 to 1991, and founded and served as abbot of Panditarama Meditation Center.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ceylon University College, under U Paññāvanta, and under Mahasi Sayadaw. He held leadership and teaching posts at the University of Mandalay, Tathāgata Meditation Center, and Dhammananda Vihara, among other institutions.

Sayadaw U Thittila worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University, later serving as a librarian at the Adyar Library and Research Centre and the Buddhist Society, and as a lecturer at the University of Yangon.
Sayagyi U Ba Khin worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Saya Thetgyi (Saya Thet Gyi) from circa 1937 to 1945 and founded the International Meditation Centre.
Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under the supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi.
Sayori Tsubota is an Indology scholar who was a doctoral student at Osaka University (attested 2020). She holds a JSPS postdoctoral fellowship post at Tohoku University (attested 2026).

Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne and has held professorial and presidential appointments at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and the Numata Center.

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed his doctorate at the Australian National University. He has held posts at ANU, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and the University of Manchester.

Sean D. Gaffney is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, also studying under Philip T. Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held a post there.

Sebastian Nehrdich is a scholar in Buddhist studies, computational studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg and Kyoto University under multiple teachers, and has held posts at Tohoku University and the University of Hamburg.
See Mui Yian is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi is a historian who completed her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held teaching and professorship posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Jamia Millia Islamia, the University of Delhi, and Ashoka University.

Seigai Omura specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo Fine Arts School under Kanō Tomonobu, subsequently serving there as an assistant professor (1896) and professor (1905).

Seiichi Mizuno worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kosaku Hamada, later serving as an assistant professor and researcher at the Kyoto Institute of the Academy of Oriental Culture, and professor at Kyoto University.

Seiichi Yagi is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1951 to 1955 and has held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology, Kanto Gakuin University, and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and law. He studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino and others, later serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo and Aichi Gakuin University.
Seiji Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa University. He later held posts at Komazawa University and Komazawa Junior College.
Seiji Kumagai specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Kyoto University (circa 2005–2008), where he later served as an associate professor from circa 2013.

Seiji Nemoto is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University from circa 1968 to 1978 and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba from circa 2006 to 2014.
Seiji Tanaka studied under Bruno Petzold. Over his career, he held posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (circa 1961–1971) and Asia University.
